goalInOwnWords: Each of six shifts I pick one machine to add to a scrap line that turns scrap into shards and then ingots. What reaches the dock is money, less whatever I spend, and I earn stars for ingots shipped (50, 100, 160). Make as much money as I can and beat my own best.
stoppedWhere: The results screen after my second game on today's yard (4100 dollars, three stars, new personal best), right after sending the survey and getting the completion code.
stoppedWhy: I had squeezed the puzzle. The offers are identical every time you replay a yard, so my second try, with a better plan, only gained 24 dollars. A third go would teach me nothing and I was past the 15 minutes. I would want a different yard, or a way to know whether 4100 is near the ceiling.

stuck.what: I needed two parts, a Splitter and a second Furnace, but get one pick a shift, and nothing says whether the parts I send back on the truck ever come back or how offers are chosen. Also when I picked the Splitter only one useless cell on the yard lit up, so I could not tell where a splitter could go or how to wire two furnaces behind it.
stuck.gotOutHow: I gambled on the Splitter, did not place it, then spent 40 dollars on New offers in shift 4 and got a Tuner instead, which fixed the furnace with one part. I never found out how to use the Splitter and sold it.

stuck.what: I dropped the Tuner next to the furnace and it refused, with a bubble saying it was a junk pile. Nothing on the yard told me before that the rubble heaps are obstacles.
stuck.gotOutHow: Read the bubble and dropped it on the cell below the furnace instead.

confused: The machine demo says a furnace ingot is worth 12 dollars, while the pick card, the price list and the job all say 24. Two prices for the same ingot.
'Ship 7 ingots a shift for a star' is never explained. I worked out that it is the pace needed over the remaining shifts to reach the next star.

Sal's 'More scrap is the next step: add a hopper' appeared when the furnace was already the limit, so a second hopper would not have helped without doubling the crusher and furnace too. It reads like the fix and is not.
The 'last shift' note ('nothing held you back, add a hopper') was still on screen after I placed the furnace, so it looked like advice about the new line when it was about the old one.
When a Splitter is picked only one cell lights up, a useless one. No idea whether a part can go on an empty cell until you try.
How offers are chosen is never said. I only learned by replaying that they are fixed for the yard, and that even the 40-dollar re-roll gives the same parts each time.
After finishing today's yard, Sal said 'First shift in the books. Try today's yard next.'
The shift 6 breakdown (six shifts plus 50 dollars sold) does not add up to the total, because the 40-dollar re-roll is not listed there. It is only explained on the final screen.
Today's yard is labelled 'practice' everywhere, so I could not tell what counts and what does not.
annoyed: Shift 1 is a throwaway: the furnace is not offered yet, so the only pick is the crusher and the shift earns 114 dollars of shards.
Sitting through an 80-second shift is dead time, I skipped every one. The watching part has little to watch once you understand it.
Junk piles are discovered only by failing a drop.
How to turn a machine or take one off the yard only appeared on screen in shift 6.
Selling spare belts is two taps for each 10 dollars, and there is no sell-all.
'Beat the day's board' has no board in this version, so the only opponent is myself.
A second try at the same yard gains almost nothing, since everything is identical.
pleased: The prices are on the table: a price list, machine demos with real dollars, times per item. I could do my own sums and they came out right.
After each shift: 'what shipped' as quantity times price equals total, and 'what held you back' in seconds, with counters on every machine.
The final ledger adds up to the dollar (163 x 24 + shards + scrap + sold parts - re-roll = 4076).
I predicted from the numbers that a second Tuner beside the crusher would get one more ingot to the dock, and the game confirmed it exactly.
The pace hint ('ship N ingots a shift for a star') once I understood it.
Skip to end of shift, 1x/2x/4x and Pause.
Replay shows 'Your best here' and says 'new personal best' with the exact difference.
Selling any unused part for 10 dollars, so no pick is wasted.
bestMoment: After shift 4 (re-rolled for 40 dollars, got the Tuner, 37 ingots exactly as my sums said) I saw that two more shifts of 37 would reach 161, one ingot over the third star, and then it held: 163 of 160. A one-ingot margin worked out from honest arithmetic.
worstMoment: Starting the second game and finding out it was identical, offer for offer. A whole replay of careful planning bought 24 dollars, and I knew I was at the ceiling.
oneChange: Tell me how good a score is. A par, or the best known score for the yard, so I can tell whether 4100 is close to the ceiling or I am missing a better build. Right now I cannot, and that is the difference between playing a third time and stopping. Also make the numbers agree (12 against 24 for an ingot).
